.: CHANGES.md product-design technical-design ./product-design: what-gets-read-aloud.md ./technical-design: article-extraction.md extraction-service.md item-contract.md markdown-units.md README.md recipes.md the-describer.md tts-service.md == technical-design/article-extraction.md:55 The API derives the spoken form from the unit's display markdown by walking its CommonMark token tree, so the display and spoken forms come from one extraction (invariant 1). A fenced code block becomes the fixed placeholder `"Code sample."`. A table's header row is spoken on its own line, then each body row as its own line of header-aware prose (`"Feature: Extraction, Status: done."`) rather than speaking pipe characters. A heading, a quote and the title unit are read as their words, without their markers. Every block inside a unit becomes its own line, so a unit carrying several paragraphs or list items never runs the last word of one into the first word of the next. A list item is its own line, with no full stop added; an ordered item keeps its `1.` at the start of the line, and nesting depth is not announced. A split list's resumed empty item (see [markdown-units](markdown-units.md)) has no spoken line at all. A task-list checkbox is stripped, and struck-through text is read as its words with no sign of the strike. Emphasis markers and link destinations are dropped throughout. == technical-design/article-extraction.md:57 A shared tail, `sanitize_spoken`, then turns any leftover emphasis or code marker that touches text into a space, so the newlines between a unit's lines survive the pass. It drops the space a marker left before punctuation, collapses whitespace, and reduces any XML-like tag shape, an opening or a closing tag around a word, to the word inside (`` to "software", `` to "div"); a lone `<` or `>` is not a tag shape and is left for the operator rule that follows. It accepts the escaped form of a tag as well, because the table linearizer reads a cell off the raw inline source, where the backslash still sits in front of the tag. A last pass turns a comparison-operator sequence into the word it stands for, longest match first: `<=` "less than or equal to", `>=` "greater than or equal to", `->` "to", `=>` "to", `<-` "from", `<<` "much less than", `>>` "much greater than", `<3` "heart", then the bare `<` "less than" and `>` "greater than". The describer's model output runs through the same tail (see [the-describer](the-describer.md)), since a JSON schema cannot forbid a marker inside its string value. == technical-design/recipes.md:15 A recipe is a script plus the declarations around it. The container selector names the element that contains the article, and everything outside the container is site chrome. The inventory names every element kind the domain's pages carry inside the container and the role each plays: a unit, inline content, a wrapper, or the title. The ignores are the selectors deliberately excluded, each with the judgement that justified it; typical ignores are ads, date stamps and share rows. Every recipe excludes footnote markers and footnote bodies, because the authoring prompts instruct it to. The prompts also require GFM markdown, the whole element passed to `toMarkdown` rather than a piece of it, one unit for a whole list even when the list holds a code block or an image, and a formula written as its alttext with no delimiter. They exclude a blockquote's attribution, a `
`, a heading self-link and a heading that repeats the title, and they keep a task list's checkboxes. See [markdown-units](markdown-units.md) for what each of those becomes in a unit's display. == technical-design/recipes.md:26 Units come back in document order, one element per unit as the recipe declares them, never overlapping: once an element is a unit, everything inside it is that unit's content. The kinds are `paragraph`, `code` and `image`. A paragraph is any flow that renders as markdown: prose, headings, quotes, lists, tables; a list is a single declared unit, even one holding a code block or an image. A paragraph or code unit carries its final display markdown, produced by the fixed conversion pass; the runtime then splits a list unit around any embedded code block or image before the units reach the API or the authoring agent's extract tool (see [markdown-units](markdown-units.md)). An image unit carries `src` and `alt` exactly as the page presents them: the recipe never invents `alt`, and the recipe resolves the domain's lazy-load conventions to produce `src`. The recipe always emits every image the article carries, even when it cannot resolve the image's src. The stages after the recipe acquire, validate, describe or drop images. == technical-design/tts-service.md:46 > Kokoro splits a paragraph string at each newline before synthesizing it and joins those pieces back with no gap between them; the 0.1-second silence only sits between two separate entries of the `paragraphs` list. So a unit whose spoken form carries several lines, such as a list's items or a table's rows (see [article-extraction](article-extraction.md)), plays as one continuous paragraph audio with no silence added between its lines. The contract does not change. `paragraphs` stays `list[str]`, one string per unit, whether that string carries one line or several. == technical-design/extraction-service.md:146 `run` executes the script inside a Dynamic Worker: the injection bundle carries cheerio, domino, and turndown with it, the article parses inside because the recipe's `$` must exist there, and what returns is JSON. The script's own `toMarkdown` calls serialize each selected element with its own tag, so Turndown sees the tag that selects its markdown rule, and a `
` with no `` child is wrapped before conversion. The validator is not part of the bundle; the mechanical checks run in the main Worker, so one implementation serves the workflow path and the agent tool path. Once validation passes, `run` splits a list unit around any nested code block or image and prepends the title unit before returning, so what crosses the boundary is already flattened (see [markdown-units](markdown-units.md)). A recipe that does not parse, throws against changed markup, or hangs until the CPU cap kills it, is a validation failure. It triggers the revision path, and its crash report takes the place of the validator report. A module that does not parse never starts the Dynamic Worker, so it cannot report itself as data; the main Worker recognises the load failure from the platform's own error, which names `recipe.js` in some runtimes and raises a bare `SyntaxError` in others. Only platform failures outside the recipe are `error` terminals: a Dynamic Worker that is unreachable, a bundle that does not load.
== technical-design/the-describer.md:32
The describer requests the response as `application/json` against that schema, so the model returns `{"spoken": "..."}` and there is nothing to parse out of prose. The parsed `spoken` then passes through `sanitize_spoken`, the same tail article prose runs through, including the rule that replaces a marker only where it touches text and the rule that speaks a comparison operator as a word (see [article-extraction](article-extraction.md)).
== product-design/what-gets-read-aloud.md:15
A listener never hears a navigation label, and a paragraph with no real words, such as a section-break ornament, is silently dropped before synthesis. The audio opens with the article's title. A heading inside the body that only repeats the title is left out, so a listener hears the title once. Some boilerplate still reaches the audio. A footer donation ask or a sponsor mention arrives as ordinary prose sentences and nothing yet tells it apart from real content.
== product-design/what-gets-read-aloud.md:22
- **A list item** reads as its own line, with no full stop added at its end. An ordered item's number is read at its start. Nesting isn't announced, so a listener hears every item at the same level, in document order.
== product-design/what-gets-read-aloud.md:28
- **A table** reads as header-aware prose, never as pipe characters. The header row is one line, then each body row is its own line ("Feature: Extraction, Status: done.").

== 11
A unit's `display` is markdown. Every recipe hands its selected elements to one shared converter rather than converting by hand ([recipes](recipes.md)), so the mapping from source to markdown is the same across every domain. The runtime then validates the recipe's declared units, splits a list around any code block or image nested inside it, and prepends the title, in that order, before anything crosses to the API or appears in the authoring agent's extract tool.
== 17
| A heading (`h1` to `h6`) | paragraph unit | ATX, `#` through `######` |
== 27
| A blockquote's `<footer>`/`<cite>` | left out | none |
== 28
| A `<dl>` | left out | none |
== 29
| Footnote references and the footnote list | left out | none |
== 30
| A heading's self-link | left out, the heading's own text stays | none |
== 34
> The runtime builds the title unit from `extraction.title` once it has every recipe-declared unit; the recipe does not select it. Building it this way is deterministic from the title the recipe already extracted, so it needs no judgement from the agent. A recipe that also selects the page's own heading as a unit still yields exactly one title: the authoring prompts tell the agent to leave out any heading that repeats the title, so the listener hears it once (see [recipes](recipes.md) and [what-gets-read-aloud](../product-design/what-gets-read-aloud.md)).
== 36
### A list split around a nested code block
== 68
The resumed part opens with an empty item at each enclosing level it needs to re-enter: the outer `2.` re-enters item B without repeating its text, and the inner `3.` picks the nested list back up at its own next number. The resumed part is valid CommonMark, and the spoken-form derivation walks the same tree the listener's page renders (see [article-extraction](article-extraction.md)).
== 84
`toMarkdown` passes the element itself, its own tag included, to Turndown with the fixed configuration (ATX headings, fenced code, `-` bullets, `---` rules) and the GFM plugin. Each Turndown rule fires only when its tag is present, so the tag selects the markdown construct: `h2` for a heading, `blockquote` for a quote, `ol` or `ul` for a list. `toMarkdown` wraps the content of a `<pre>` with no `<code>` child in `<code>` before conversion, so every `<pre>` becomes a fenced block.
== 86
The same validator runs at authoring, revision and extraction, against the real element paths the recipe declared ([recipes](recipes.md)). Only once validation is clean does the runtime split a list unit that holds a code block or an image, at any nesting depth. The split yields a list part, then the code or image unit, then the rest of the list, in document order. `toMarkdown` converts each list part with its own list tag intact. The runtime prepends the title unit last. What the workflow returns, and what an authoring or revising agent's extract tool shows, is this same flattened list ([extraction-service](extraction-service.md)).
== 89
> The validator's nesting check flags any two units whose paths sit inside one another, and a list-part clone that the split produces has no path, because the clone was never part of the parsed article tree. Validating the declared units first, while they are still elements at real positions, means every path the validator checks is real, and a split part never needs one.
== 92
> Inventory and leftover-text checks confirm that every element in the container is accounted for and that no readable text was dropped. Neither confirms that a unit's markdown syntax, such as a heading's `#`, a quote's `>` or a list's numbering, survived the conversion.
== 95
> An item pulled out of its enclosing `<ol>` or `<ul>` and converted alone loses that context. Turndown's list rule reads the parent `<ol>` or `<ul>` to number or bullet an item, so an item converted alone comes out with no ordinal and no bullet. The runtime instead keeps every surviving list part inside a clone of the original list's own tag, so each part still carries something to number or bullet from.
== 98
> `sanitize_spoken` has a rule for each markdown marker Turndown can emit and no rule for a dollar sign, so a delimiter would reach the audio as a literal character. The alttext carries no delimiter at all instead, and reads as plain words in both the display and the spoken form.
== 102
- **Telling code apart from a non-code `<pre>`.** `toMarkdown` treats every `<pre>` as code and wraps it in `<code>` before conversion; nothing distinguishes a `<pre>` used for plain preformatted layout.
== 104
- **The display of a table with no header row.** The GFM table stays whatever Turndown produces for it; the header-aware linearization a table's spoken form gets ([article-extraction](article-extraction.md)) has no counterpart in the display markdown.
